q: Explain the significance of Quinta do Noval Nacional.
accept: ungrafted vines tiny production legendary vintage port
ans: A small ungrafted parcel producing minuscule quantities of legendary Vintage Port, declared only in exceptional years
exp: The 1931 and 1963 are among Port's most coveted bottles.

q: Which grape gives Bairrada its sparkling wines and what method is used?
ans: Baga (and Bical/Maria Gomes), by traditional method
exp: Portugal's oldest sparkling tradition, dating to the 1890s.

q: Late Bottled Vintage Port must be bottled within which window after the harvest?
opts: Between the second and third year
Between the fourth and sixth year
Between the third and fifth year
Between the seventh and tenth year
exp: Precisely: between 1 July of the fourth year and 31 December of the sixth year after the harvest. Vintage Port's window is far earlier — 1 July of the second year to 30 June of the third — which is the distinction being tested. LBV therefore does the cask ageing on the shipper's premises rather than in your cellar; filtered versions are stable and ready on release, while 'unfiltered' or 'bottle-matured' LBV throws a deposit, needs decanting and behaves like a small Vintage.

q: Which 'Indication of Age' categories may a Tawny Port carry, and what does the number actually mean?
accept: 10 20 30 40 and 50 years an approved average age not a minimum
ten twenty thirty forty and fifty year tawnies judged on average age
the age indications are 10 20 30 40 50 and describe an average
ans: 10, 20, 30, 40 and — since the IVDP added the tier in 2022 — 50 years old. The figure is not a minimum age nor the age of the youngest component but a target style: an average age approved by the IVDP's tasting chamber for a blend drawn from many vintages
exp: Older textbooks stop at 40; the 50-year tier is current law and now sits on shelves. Two traps follow. First, the number is a style judgement made by a tasting panel, so two 20-year-olds from different houses can differ sharply. Second, do not confuse an aged Tawny with a Colheita, which is a tawny from one declared vintage, cask-aged a minimum of seven years and labelled with both the harvest and the bottling date.

q: Which producer makes Monfortino, Barolo's most storied riserva, from Francia in Serralunga?
exp: Roberto Conterno continues it: botti, years of cask, released when ready.

q: Sassicaia's founding family and first commercial vintage are:
exp: Cuttings reputedly from Lafite; its own DOC (Bolgheri Sassicaia) since 2013.

q: Vega Sicilia 'Único' typically reaches market after roughly how long?
exp: A decade-plus of cask and bottle; Reserva Especial is a multi-vintage blend.

q: Name the Rioja bodega whose Viña Tondonia whites release after decades and whose cellars grow their own mold.
exp: Founded 1877; nothing has changed on purpose.

q: Which German estate's Scharzhofberger Trockenbeerenauslese is the world's most expensive regularly produced white wine?
Henri Jayer's most mythologized bottling was from which premier cru?
exp: Reclaimed from artichokes after the war; Emmanuel Rouget continues the holdings.

q: Screaming Eagle's debut vintage, made by Heidi Barrett, was:
exp: 1992, released 1995; Jean Phillips' Oakville estate became the cult benchmark.

q: Which Australian wine did Max Schubert create in secret after a 1950 Bordeaux trip?
exp: Management ordered it stopped in 1957; he kept making it in hiding. First commercial: 1952.

q: Henschke's Hill of Grace vineyard grows beside a church in which GI region, with vines dating to the 1860s?
exp: The 'Grandfathers' block is pre-phylloxera Shiraz — single vineyard, unlike multi-region Grange.

ans: Quintarelli–Amarone · Clos Rougeard–Saumur-Champigny · Vega Sicilia–Ribera · Huet–Vouvray
exp: The Foucault brothers' Rougeard turned Loire Cab Franc into a collectible.

q: Ridge Monte Bello grows at ~800 m in which mountain AVA?
exp: Limestone under Cabernet; fifth at the 1976 Paris tasting, first at the 2006 thirtieth-anniversary rematch.

q: Which Priorat pioneer's 'L'Ermita' revived the region alongside Clos Mogador's René Barbier?
exp: The 1989 'Gratallops gang'; old-vine Garnacha on llicorella.
